statement.p: Find a number a so that the change of variables s=x+ay, t=y transforms the integral \int\int_R \,dx\,dy over the parallelogram R in the xy-plane with vertices (0,0), (24,0), (-28,11), (-4,11) into an integral \int\int_T \left\vert \frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(s,t)}\right\vert\,ds\,dt over a rectangle T in the st-plane.

static.solution:
x = s-at, y=t. The four edges of R are y=0, y=11, y=-\frac{11}{28} x, y=-\frac{11}{28} (x-24). The change of variables transforms the edges to t=0, t=11, t=-\frac{11}{28} s + \frac{11}{28} at, t=-\frac{11}{28} s + \frac{11}{28} at + \frac{66}{7}. These are equations for the edges of a rectangle in the st-plane if the last two are of the form: s=(\hbox{Constant}). This happens when the t terms drop out, or a=\frac{28}{11}. With a=\frac{28}{11} the change of variables gives \int\int_T \left\vert \frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(s,t)}\right\vert \,ds\,dt over the rectangle T: 0\le t \le 11, 0\le s\le 24.
The jacobian \left\vert\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(s,t)}\right\vert is \left\vert\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(s,t)}\right\vert = \left\vert\begin{array}{cc} 1 \amp -\frac{28}{11} \\ 0 \amp 1 \end{array} \right\vert = 1.
